h: שׁוּשַׁן פּוּרִים, מַאֲמָר א׳ Shushan Purim — Maamar Aleph

p: "The rose of Yaakov exulted and rejoiced
בִּרְאוֹתָם יַחַד תְּכֵלֶת מָרְדֳּכַי [פִּיּוּט לְאַחַר קְרִיאַת הַמְּגִילָּה].
when they together beheld Mordechai's techeiles" (piyut after the reading of the Megillah).
מְיֻסָּד עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר [אֶסְתֵּר ח, טו]
is founded on what is said (Esther 8:15):
"And Mordechai went out from before the King
in royal garments of techeiles," etc.,
"and the city of Shushan exulted and rejoiced."
as written in Pri Etz Chaim
and it alludes to Knesses Yisrael,
which is like a rose among the thorns,
as stated in the holy Zohar
מָה שׁוֹשַׁנָּה אִית בָּהּ תְּלֵיסַר עָלִין
"Just as the rose has thirteen petals,
up to "the spirit of Elokim" there are thirteen words,
corresponding to the thirteen attributes of mercy,
up to the words "and the spirit of Elokim,"
which alludes to the spirit of Mashiach
for this was the ultimate intent
of Creation with respect to Adam HaRishon.
until "And Elokim said, Let there be light" —
corresponding to the five strong leaves
that is, corresponding to the five gevuros
that are sweetened through the light,
which is the light of teshuvah,
and through this it can be rectified
And to this alludes the word "and the city,"
corresponding to the five of the rose;
and together with the word Shushan
alludes to the Jews in Shushan,
and they are the rabbis and the Sanhedrin
who know how to intercalate years
to the aspect of the rose mentioned above,
one may say, in simple terms,
on the verse "And to Binyamin he gave
that Mordechai was destined to descend from him,
who went out from before the King
and these are the garments of the mitzvos
that are made in Gan Eden,
as stated in the holy Zohar
this is the holy spirit, etc.;
as it is written, "And Mordechai went out from before the King
It alludes that he went out from before the King,
for he was clothed in five garments of the Kingdom of Heaven;
and techeiles alludes to the hue of yirah,
(and it was explained in Parshas Vayigash, maamar 7,
and therefore he mentions as primary
which alludes to "The beginning of wisdom
to the Jews who are in Shushan
to do according to today's decree" (Esther 9:13) —
from what the King said to her,
"And what is your further request? It shall be done" (ibid. 12),
that it was surely the will of the King of kings,
the Holy One, blessed is He,
to make some further rectification for the generations;
that one more day must be added
in Shushan, for the illumination of the miracle.
The inner meaning of the matter will be understood
from what they said in the Gemara (there, 11a):
One: "A roaring lion" — this is Nevuchadnetzar;
"and a ravenous bear" — this is Achashverosh;
"over a poor people" — this is Yisrael,
because of the sloth that Yisrael had,
that they did not engage in Torah,
נַעֲשָׂה שׂוֹנְאוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָךְ
the "enemy" of the Holy One, blessed is He, became poor —
and mach means only poor, etc.,
וְאֵין מְקָרֶה אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and mekareh means only the Holy One, blessed is He,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [תְּהִלִּים קד, ג] הַמְקָרֶה בַמַּיִם עֲלִיּוֹתָיו.
as it says (Tehillim 104:3), "Who roofs His upper chambers with water."
Seemingly there is no connection at all
between this opening and the matter of the Megillah,
no hint at all of Achashverosh and Haman.
וְיוּבַן זֶה עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
This will be understood from what they said
"Fortunate are you who sow beside all waters,
מְשַׁלְּחֵי רֶגֶל הַשּׁוֹר וְהַחֲמוֹר [יְשַׁעְיָה לב, כ]
who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey" (Yeshayahu 32:20) —
you engage in Torah and in acts of kindness;
their inclination is delivered into their hands, etc.;
And as for the allusion to the yetzer hara,
Rashi (s.v. Meshalchei) and Tosafos (s.v. Yitzram) wrote
that it is from the word "foot,"
for the yetzer hara is called a wayfarer,
כִּדְכְתִיב [שְׁמוּאֵל ב יב, ד] וַיָּבֹא הֵלֶךְ וְגוֹ׳
as it is written (II Shmuel 12:4), "And a wayfarer came," etc.
And chiefly it alludes to the kelipah of Amalek,
which is called a wayfarer, like a traveler,
for this is the first way of the yetzer hara:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [דְּבָרִים כה, יח] אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
as it is said (Devarim 25:18), "who happened upon you on the way,"
and he is the first of the kelipah.
that the main power of Amalek
is when they slacken their hands
is used in the Yerushalmi and the Midrashim
for the mitzvah of tzedakah and acts of kindness.
"Yeshno" — they are asleep from the mitzvos;
He said to him: "There are Rabbis among them" —
he said to Him: "They are one people" —
that in this too there is slackness of hands.
Therefore the Men of the Great Assembly instituted
that caused the kelipah of Amalek to overpower them:
to repair the flaw of stinginess
in the mitzvah of tzedakah and kindness.
And to this alludes the opening:
"and a ravenous bear" — this is Achashverosh,
דִּכְתִיב [עֶזְרָא ד, ו] וּבְמַלְכוּת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְגוֹ׳
as it is written (Ezra 4:6), "And in the reign of Achashverosh," etc.,
גַּם כֵּן לְבַטֵּל בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
also to halt the building of the Beis HaMikdash.
"over a poor people" — this is Yisrael,
in every place and at every time.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה שְׁלִיטַת עֲמָלֵק
And through this came the dominion of Amalek,
which is Haman, as mentioned above.
the destruction and halting of the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
for the essential building of the Beis HaMikdash
is through the deeds of the mitzvos,
whereas of the deeds of the tzaddikim
"the Sanctuary, my Lord, which Your hands established" —
It is along the lines of what they said
even a single one of Yisrael
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [שְׁמוֹת כה, ב] מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ
as it is said (Shemos 25:2), "From every man
That is, through the generosity of his heart
"By what shall the horn of Yisrael be raised?
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי נְדִיבוּת לֵב לִצְדָקָה
that is, through generosity of heart for tzedakah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם ד״ה אָמַר).
And the mitzvah of feasting and gladness of Purim
of sloth in the study of Torah,
along the lines of what is said (Mishlei 15:15):
"All the days of the poor man are bad,"
which alludes to one poor in understanding,
"There is no poor man except in knowledge";
this is one who does not take to heart
the preciousness of words of Torah —
and this means even Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim
and it alludes that even Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim,
which were given for engaging in Torah,
[רְאֵה יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שַׁבָּת פט״ו ה״ג עח, א]
will not help one poor in understanding
one who engages in words of Torah constantly,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רוּת רַבָּה ה, טו)
along the lines of what they said (Rus Rabbah 5:15)
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר [רוּת ג, ז] וַיִּיטַב לִבּוֹ
on what is said (Rus 3:7), "And his heart was merry" —
that he engaged in words of Torah.
along the lines of what is said (Mishlei 9:5),
"And drink of the wine I have mixed";
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה עַל לִבּוֹ
and by setting the words of Torah upon his heart,
from this the gladness also comes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [תְּהִלִּים צז, יא] וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה
as it is said (Tehillim 97:11), "And for the upright of heart, gladness"
(and it was explained at the fourteenth of Adar Rishon, maamar 2).
And to this alludes the second opening:
because of the sloth that Yisrael had,
that they did not engage in Torah,
נַעֲשָׂה שׂוֹנְאוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָךְ
the "enemy" of the Holy One, blessed is He, became poor;
וְאֵין מְקָרֶה אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and mekareh means only the Holy One, blessed is He,
as it says, "Who roofs His upper chambers with water."
And why they designated here His Name, may He be blessed,
יוּבַן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
will be understood from what they said in the holy Zohar
Rabbi Shimon said: Above and below.
The accusation against the Holy One, blessed is He,
Moshe said: I will prepare myself
For the matter of the battle below in practice
in the deeds of the mitzvos, as mentioned above;
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה מוּכָן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְהַכְנִיעוֹ
and for this Yehoshua was prepared to subdue him,
for he was of the seed of Yosef,
who was careful in the deeds of the mitzvos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [בְּרֵאשִׁית מז, יב] וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף וְגוֹ׳.
as it is said (Bereishis 47:12), "And Yosef sustained," etc.
is that the accusation should take effect Above,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה [אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה ז, יג]
as they said in Midrash Rabbah (Esther Rabbah 7:13)
וּמָרְדֳּכַי יָדַע אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר נַעֲשָׂה
"And Mordechai knew all that had been done,"
that they informed him that the decree had been sealed
And this came only from sloth
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הֶבֶל דַּל הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
for through even the slight breath of words of Torah
a partition and a ceiling is formed
so that his accusation does not ascend Above.
because of the sloth Yisrael had in Torah,
that is, the ceiling and partition
against the accusation, formed by the Torah,
as it is said, "Who roofs His upper chambers with water,"
"I will prepare myself for the battle Above,"
to receive the Torah for Yisrael,
and this would serve to annul the accusation
and to be a ceiling and partition before it,
Now it is stated in the Gemara (Megillah 12a):
of the feast of that wicked one."
"If so, those in Shushan should be killed," etc.
אָמַר לָהֶם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַצֶּלֶם וְכוּ׳
He said to them: "Because they bowed to the image," etc.
correspond to the two flaws mentioned above.
corresponds to the blemish of neglecting the mitzvos,
and in this the blemish was in all of Yisrael,
and it was rectified on the thirteenth,
and they rested on the fourteenth.
And the second blemish, partaking of his feast,
that is, among the Rabbis and talmidei chachamim,
who were all at this feast
because there were prepared for them
לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹן אִישׁ וָאִישׁ [אֶסְתֵּר א, ח]
"To do according to the will of every man" (Esther 1:8) —
according to the will of Mordechai, etc.;
and they were compelled to this
and there was no prohibition at all in the matter.
It was only that they "partook of" his feast, precisely —
and they did not say that they "ate";
only because they felt in it
וְזֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי עַצְלוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
and this came through sloth in words of Torah,
כִּי מִי שֶׁדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה נִקְשָׁרִים בְּלִבּוֹ
for one in whose heart the words of Torah are bound
also tomorrow according to today's decree.
וְהִנֵּה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פח, א)
that at the time of Matan Torah
they tied for each one of Yisrael
and one corresponding to "we will hear."
is the actual performance of the mitzvos,
and "we will hear" is engagement in Torah,
that the heart should listen to words of Torah.
So said the Holy One, blessed is He:
שְׁנֵי כוֹסוֹת מְזַגְתֶּם בְּסִינַי נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע
"You mixed two cups at Sinai, 'we will do' and 'we will hear';
For the crown of "we will hear"
נִשְׁאַר לָנוּ עַל יְדֵי עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה
remained ours through engagement in Torah;
and on this basis the custom spread in Yisrael
to wear on Shabbos on the head
a hat distinct in its form
from the one worn on weekdays,
which is not so with the other garments,
and not in a different form
This is because the hat alludes
that was given to us on Shabbos
from the aspect of "we will hear," as mentioned above.
And based on this, some have the custom
also on the fifteenth of Adar
and it is to allude to our words above,
because in Shushan the miracle was effected on it
for the renewal of "we will hear" in words of Torah,
as they said (Shabbos, ibid.): "They accepted it anew
in the days of Achashverosh, out of love for the miracle."
which was the rectification of the flaw
of sloth in words of Torah,
And through the eradication of Amalek
the crown of "we will hear" was restored to us,

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah and Purim, chapter 6 — “Esther has the numerical value of shoshanah. Esther also equals 671 less ten. This is the mystery of the inward point itself that is concealed, the mystery of the yod of Adonai; for Adonai, when spelled out in full, has the numerical value 671.” Both names have the numerical value 661. The identification of the rose with the congregation of Israel is developed in the opening of the Zohar, quoted next.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 1a (Introduction) — “Rabbi Chizkiyah opened: ‘Like a rose among thorns.’ What is the rose? The congregation of Israel. Just as a rose among thorns has red and white, so the congregation of Israel has judgment and mercy. Just as a rose has thirteen petals, so the congregation of Israel has thirteen attributes of mercy surrounding it on every side. So, from the first mention of God, He brought forth thirteen words to surround and guard the congregation of Israel.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 1a (Introduction) — “Afterward it is mentioned a second time. Why a second time? To bring forth five strong leaves that surround the rose. These five are called salvations; they are five gates. Of this mystery it is written, ‘I shall raise the cup of salvations.’ This is the cup of blessing. The cup of blessing must rest upon five fingers and no more, just as the rose rests upon five strong leaves, the image of five fingers.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayigash 7:1 — “Blue signifies awe.... White is expounded from chivvar, as they said: white wool. This alludes to love: the aspect of Jacob and Joseph—Joseph, who said, ‘I fear God,’ and Jacob, mercy.... Blue and white are judgment and mercy.... The two crowns correspond to Wisdom and Understanding: the crown corresponds to Wisdom, and the wrap to Understanding.... Through the union of Wisdom and Understanding, brain and heart—when the wisdom in the brain enters Understanding in the heart—one attains Knowledge, which is the inward aspect of the Crown.... These are the crowns Israel attained at the giving of the Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Esther 9:12-13 — “The king said to Queen Esther: ‘In Shushan the capital the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and Haman’s ten sons.... What further request have you? It shall be done.’ Esther said: ‘If it is good to the king, let it be granted tomorrow also to the Jews in Shushan to act according to today’s law, and let Haman’s ten sons be hung upon the tree.’”

paragraphs.text: Megillah 11a — “Resh Lakish opened his exposition of this scroll from here: ‘A roaring lion and a ravenous bear—a wicked ruler over a poor people.’ ‘A roaring lion’ is Nebuchadnezzar.... ‘A ravenous bear’ is Ahasuerus.... ‘A wicked ruler’ is Haman. ‘Over a poor people’—these are Israel, who were poor in commandments.”

paragraphs.text: Megillah 11a — “Rabbi Elazar opened his exposition from here: ‘Through laziness the ceiling sags.’ Because of Israel’s laziness in not engaging in Torah, the Holy One’s enemy became impoverished. ‘Impoverished’ means poor, as it says, ‘If he is too poor for the valuation.’ ‘Ceiling’ refers only to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, ‘Who roofs His upper chambers with water.’” The expression “the Holy One’s enemy” is the Talmud’s reverential euphemism. Rav Tzadok later develops the image of Torah as a roof blocking accusation.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 146a — “‘All the days of the poor are bad.’ But are there not Sabbaths and festivals? This accords with Shmuel, for Shmuel said: ‘A change of habitual eating is the beginning of intestinal illness.’” The Gemara explains how even festive eating can trouble the materially poor person. Rav Tzadok rereads “poor” through Nedarim as poverty of understanding, so that even a day intended for Torah fails to gladden him.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 12a — “‘To do according to the wish of each man’—Rava said: To do according to the wish of Mordechai and Haman. Mordechai is called ‘a man’: ‘There was a Jewish man’; Haman is called ‘a man’: ‘A man, an adversary and enemy.’” The Gemara identifies the two “men.” The detailed claim here about kosher provisions and the distinction between eating and enjoying the banquet belong to Rav Tzadok’s explanation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillas Yesharim, ch. 26, §§7, 10–13 — “The person who sanctifies himself with his Creator’s holiness finds even his bodily deeds becoming actual matters of holiness. ... Such a person is himself reckoned as a Tabernacle, a Temple, and an altar. ... The Divine Presence rests upon them as it rested in the Temple; hence the food they eat is like an offering ascending upon the altar’s fires. ... The food and drink consumed by the holy person are elevated, as though actually offered upon the altar. ... This does not mean that Torah scholars should be inflamed with desire for food and drink, Heaven forbid, filling their throats as one stuffs a glutton. Rather, Torah scholars whose ways and deeds are holy are literally like a Temple and an altar, because the Divine Presence rests upon them as it literally rested in the Temple, and what is offered to them is as though offered upon the altar.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Ramchal supplies a precise distinction behind Rav Tzadok’s account of the scholars’ banquet: bodily consumption can become actual sacred service, while appetite for one’s own pleasure remains a different motive. His description concerns an attained state of holiness. It clarifies how Torah bound within the heart could transform a permitted meal, and why Rav Tzadok locates the failure in enjoying the wicked king’s banquet rather than in its food being forbidden.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88a — “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel put ‘we shall do’ before ‘we shall hear,’ six hundred thousand ministering angels came, and each bound two crowns upon every Israelite—one corresponding to ‘we shall do,’ and one to ‘we shall hear.’ Once Israel sinned, twelve hundred thousand destroying angels descended and removed them.”
